title: Carbon pricing on shipping

definition.text: Carbon pricing on shipping charges ships for the greenhouse gases they emit.

facts.text: Maritime transport makes up 3% of global greenhouse gas emissions.
A carbon price is meant to close the cost gap between heavy fuel oil and low-carbon fuels, breaking a stand-off where fuel suppliers and shipowners each wait for the other to move first.
In 2023 the EU Emissions Trading System was extended to shipping, and the International Maritime Organization set a goal of net-zero shipping emissions by around 2050.
An IMO pricing scheme would be the first global carbon pricing system; countries including China, Brazil and South Africa oppose it as unfair to developing countries.

contested_note: Stakeholders disagree over whether shipping carbon revenue should be spent within shipping or as general climate finance.

title: Energy Innovation and Carbon Dividend Act
article: Energy Innovation and Carbon Dividend Act of 2019

definition.text: The Energy Innovation and Carbon Dividend Act was a US House bill to charge a fee on carbon at the point of extraction and return the money to citizens.

facts.text: The fee would start at $15 per tonne of CO2-equivalent and rise each year by $10 or more.
It was based on the Citizens' Climate Lobby's carbon fee and dividend proposal.
It gained 86 cosponsors in 2019 but never got a vote.

notes: Excluded: a single US bill that was never passed; useful only as an example under Carbon fee and dividend.

title: Energy Tax Act

definition.text: The Energy Tax Act of 1978 was a US law using taxes and tax credits to cut oil and gas demand during the 1970s energy crisis.

facts.text: It gave tax credits for home solar, wind and geothermal energy and for business renewable equipment.
It created the Gas Guzzler Tax on passenger cars with low EPA-rated fuel economy, paid by the maker or importer.
Critics argue the tax helped SUVs dominate because trucks, SUVs and minivans were exempt.

notes: Excluded: single-country law; the Gas Guzzler Tax may serve as an example under Feebate or Energy tax.

definition.text: An energy tax is a tax that raises the price of energy, usually charged on the fuels themselves.

facts.text: Energy taxes are the most commonly used environmental taxes in the world.
They can be levied on producing, distributing or using energy, mainly fossil fuels and sometimes electricity.
Arguments for them include cutting fiscal deficits as well as reducing pollution.
A weakness is that they impose costs in reduced economic output and jobs.
Energy taxes and the removal of fossil fuel subsidies can be seen as pricing carbon implicitly, because they change fossil fuel prices.
A US BTU tax proposed in 1993 to tax fuels by heat content passed the House but was rejected by the Senate after heavy lobbying.
